name: Quantization Parameter Analysis
description: Analyzes video codec QP values for compression consistency — re-encoded deepfakes show QP anomalies.
mechanism:
This method analyzes quantization parameter (QP) patterns for video forensic detection:

1. **QP Map Extraction**: The per-macroblock quantization parameter is extracted from the video bitstream. The QP map reveals how the encoder allocated quality across the frame — lower QP (higher quality) for important/complex regions, higher QP (lower quality) for simpler regions.

2. **QP Distribution Analysis**: The QP distribution across the frame is analyzed. Authentic single-encoded video shows QP values following the encoder's rate-control algorithm — smooth QP variation correlated with content complexity. Re-encoded video (manipulation + re-encoding) shows QP distributions influenced by two encoding passes.

3. **QP-Content Consistency**: The relationship between QP and local content complexity is verified. In normal encoding, complex regions (edges, texture) receive lower QP. Manipulated regions may show QP-content mismatches — the second encoder's QP decisions may not optimally match the inserted content.

4. **Double Quantization Detection**: When video is decoded, manipulated, and re-encoded, characteristic double-quantization artifacts appear in the QP and DCT coefficient distributions. The method detects periodicities in DCT histograms that indicate the original QP, revealing the encoding history.

5. **Temporal QP Pattern Analysis**: QP allocation across frames follows the encoder's rate control model — I-frames typically get lower QP than P/B-frames. The method analyzes temporal QP patterns for anomalies. Manipulated video segments may show QP pattern breaks where the manipulation disrupted the original rate control.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models
